NEBaseChanger

ABOUT   HELP   RESOURCES   TROUBLESHOOT  
v2.11.0
NEBaseChanger assists in the design of primers for site-directed mutagenesis experiments using the Q5 Site-Directed Mutagenesis Kit. Additional resources for NEBaseChanger, including related products, videos, tutorials, and application notes are available here.  

  • Need help getting started? Please check the Help page and this video tutorial.
  • Need help troubleshooting your site-directed mutagenesis experiment? Try the new Troubleshooting Module

1. Enter new sequence.

Partial Sequence Help
Select partial if only a portion of the complete circular sequence is entered.

Selecting the "Partial" checkbox tells NEBaseChanger that it should not assume
a complete circular sequence, allowing the entry of a much shorter sequence.
However, partial sequences will need to include sufficient sequence flanking the mutation site,
currently set at a minimum of 35 nt 5′ and 25 nt 3′. Mutations will be prohibited
from being too close to the ends of the provided partial sequence fragment
and cannot span the ends of the fragment.
or paste/type sequence below.

           
Length: 0 bp   

2. Select input mode and set mutations.

Input Sequence
Enter a DNA sequence by copying and pasting it into the sequence text area
or uploading a file from your computer. Acceptable formats for the DNA sequence are:

raw -- plain text without IDs and descriptions or numbers
FASTA -- first line consisting of ">ID optional description"
GenBank -- standard GenBank (LOCUS and ORIGIN lines expected).

Selecting the "Use Reverse Complement" checkbox instructs NEBaseChanger to use
the reverse complement of the sequence entered in the sequence text area.
Selecting the "Partial" checkbox tells NEBaseChanger that it should not assume
a complete circular sequence, allowing the entry of a much shorter sequence.
However, partial sequences will need to include sufficient sequence flanking the mutation site,
currently set at a minimum of 35 nt 5′ and 25 nt 3′. Mutations will be prohibited
from being too close to the ends of the provided partial sequence fragment
and cannot span the ends of the fragment.
Input Mode
After entering the starting plasmid sequence, choose either "AA Point Mutation",
"Indel/Substitution", "Batch", or "Legacy". Point mutation mode is most convenient
if the mutagenesis is limited to one or more single codons, whereas the general
Indel/Substitution mode works with larger (and smaller) single insertions and substitutions
and also allows deletions. Batch mode is designed for a longer list of mutations
and allows mixing of point and indel styles of entry.

Legacy mode is intended to emulate NEBaseChanger V1 and produce results that are consistent
with the parameters used in V1. Principally, the minimum primer length is reset to 18 nt
and insertions are always in the 5′ tails. Legacy mode has a simpler interface
that will be familiar to users of V1, but it is limited in functionality.
Legacy Input Help
LEGACY MODE ---

Legacy mode is intended to emulate NEBaseChanger V1 and produce results
that are consistent with the parameters used in V1. Principally, the minimum
primer length is reset to 18nt and insertions are always in the 5′ tails.

Insert/delete/substitute operations require a 5' flanking position (start),
3' flanking position (end); the target sequence to be mutatated is
between the start and end positions.
This differs from V1 where substitutions
and deletions were identified by the coordinates of the target itself.

In addition to manualy setting the start/end coordinates of the target,
the target sequence may be selected by click and drag (text selection)
in the DNA sequence row. For insertions, clicking between two bases will select the
proper flanking bases. The target sequence may also be located using the search field.

For deletions, leave the replacement sequence blank.

Ambiguous base codes can be entered in the replacement sequence (N,Y,S,W, etc)
and will be expanded combinatorialy.

For example, a replacement sequence containing NS will be expanded to 8 sequences
containing: AC, CC, GC, TC, AG, CG, GG, and TG, generating 8 primer pairs.
InDel Input Help
Insert/delete/substitute (indel) operations require a 5' flanking position (start),
3' flanking position (end), and a replacement sequence. The target sequence to be
replaced is between the start and end positions.

To delete a sequence, leave the replacement sequence blank.

To insert a sequence, the start and end should be consecutive positions.
The replacement sequence will be inserted between them.

For example, if start/end is 234/239 and the replacement sequence is ACGT,
the operation will substitute the sequence between bases 234 and 239 with ACGT.

Ambiguous base codes can be entered in the replacement sequence (N,Y,S,W, etc)
and will be expanded combinatorialy.

For example, a replacement sequence containing NS will be expanded to 8 sequences
containing: AC, CC, GC, TC, AG, CG, GG, and TG, generating 8 primer pairs.
AA Point Mutation Input Help
First, enter the start position of the ORF, either directly by entering the coordinate
or by clicking in the DNA sequence row of the codon view. Setting the ORF start
position will highlight the ORF. Changing it keeps the mutations you've entered;
any that no longer match the new frame are skipped, with a warning.

Next, enter one or more mutations of the form [old AA][codon #][new AA],
for example, M2A, F32H, C45Y, etc. The codon # is relative to the selected
ORF start. Optionally, specify the exact triplet replacement by appending
a colon followed by the triplet, for example, M2G:GGG, A34F:TTC. Exact triplets,
will override automatic selection. Multiple mutations can be entered, separated by spaces, commas or semicolons.

Clicking on an amino acid in the codon view will initiate a dialog to select the replacement
amino acid, including the exact triplet, and will add it to the list of mutations.

The old AA is checked, but processing is not halted if the old AA does not match
the indicated codon #. The codon number takes presidence. Also, the ORF start
can be set arbitrarily and is not checked for validity.
Batch Input Help
Batch input mode allows multiple command line style operations to be applied
to the currently loaded sequence. It is intended to facilitate the entry
of large numbers of mutations on a single input sequence.

Batch commands can be loaded from a text file, pasted into the text area, or typed in directly.

All batch input operates on the currently loaded sequence. Each batch command
should be on a separate line. The following commands are supported in Batch mode:
1. ORF: [start]
2. [old AA][codon #][new AA]:[triplet]
3. [ID] [start] [end] [replacement]

ORF: [start]
Specifies the coordinate of the first base of the ORF. Required for subsequent AA point mutations.

Examples:
ORF: 1256
ORF: 2

[start] must be a positive number in the range 1 to sequence length.
All subsequent point mutation commands will be relative to the specified ORF start.


[old AA][codon #][new AA]:[triplet]
Specifies an AA point mutation at a specific codon.

Examples:
A2F
A2F:TTT

[Old AA] and [new AA] are single letter codes for the current and mutated AA, respectively.
[codon #] counts triplets from the last specified ORF start coordinate.
The :[triplet] specifier is optional. If provided, it should consist of
a colon followed immediately by the triplet replacement sequence. If not specified,
(leave off the colon) the replacement triplet will be the codon with the highest usage
in E. coli K12. Exact triplets, will override automatic selection.


[ID] [start] [end] [replacement]
Specifies a general indel/substitution operation.

Examples:
ID1 234 239 deletes the sequence between bases 234 and 239.
ID2 234 239 ACGT substitutes ACGT for the sequence between bases 234 and 239.
ID3 234 235 ACGT inserts ACGT between bases 234 and 235.

[Start] and [end] are the base positions flanking the target sequence
to be replaced. If [replacement] is omitted, the target sequence will be deleted.
To insert a sequence, [start] and [end] should be consecutive positions.


Any ambiguous base codes (N,Y,S,W, etc) will be expanded combinatorialy
unless "Preserve degenerate bases" is checked.
For example, a replacement sequence containing NS will be expanded to 8 sequences
containing: AC, CC, GC, TC, AG, CG, GG, and TG, generating 8 primer pairs.

The following is an example of a valid set of batch commands:

ORF: 100
M1Y
A42S
P24F:TTT
setA 200 205 NNA
InSetB 400 401 AACGGTGTN
Site1 100 105 ACGT
D1 1000 1200
setE 1800 200 ATNCG

Confine mutations to primer tails
If the "Confine mutations to primer 5′ tails" option is selected,
the replacement sequence will always be attached to the 5′ end
of the primers, regardless of the length of the substitution.
Normally, for substitutions, if the target region is longer than 6 nucleotides,
the substitution sequence will be split between the two primers, attached
to the 5′ end of the primers as non-annealing tails. The 5′ ends
of the annealing portions of the primers align with the edges of the target region.
If the target region encompasses 6 or fewer nucleotides, the replacement sequence
will be placed in the forward primer with 10 or more bases of annealing sequence
flanking the inserted bases.
This option is always on while "Preserve degenerate bases" is selected.
Preserve degenerate bases
This option keeps degenerate/ambiguous base codes in the primer sequence when selecting
the amino acid "X" representing all possible amino acids, in targeted saturation mutagenesis.
Normally, the ambiguous bases (NNK) are expanded to create 32 primer pairs with only canonical bases.
With this option selected, only one primer pair will be generated containing "NNK".
This option is currently only compatible with mutations confined to the 5′ primer tail.
Merge multiple point mutations
This option merges point mutations to keep them within a single primer pair.
Mutations are entered normally in the form [old AA][codon #][new AA],
for example, M1A, D3H, C4Y, etc., separated by spaces, commas or semicolons.

If the mutations are close together, generally not separated by more than 6 bases,
the mutations are merged and treated as a sequence replacement operation.
In the example above, all 3 mutations would be embedded in a single primer pair.

This option is currently only compatible with mutations confined to the 5′ primer tail.
Codon selection: codon usage
If Codon Selection is set to "codon usage", NEBaseChanger will use codon usage tables
for E. coli K12 to select the codon that has the highest usage. If multiple codons have
the same usage frequency, the choice between them is not defined and could be random.
Codon selection: parsimony
If Codon Selection is set to "parsimony", NEBaseChanger will select the codon that has
the maximum parsimony defined here as the fewest base changes relative to the codon
being replaced. If multiple codons have the same minimum distance, the choice between them
is not defined and could be random.
Generate NEBuilder HiFi primers
By selecting this option, NEBaseChanger will generate primer pairs compatible with
the NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix to simplify the execution of multiple
site-directed mutagenesis in a single reaction.

Details are available here.
Mutation One-Letter-Codes
Enter one or more mutations of the form
[old AA][codon #][new AA], for example, M2A, F32H, C45Y, etc.
Optionally, specify the exact triplet replacement by appending a colon followed by the triplet,
for example, M2G:GGG, A34F:TTC. Exact triplets, when specified, will override automatic selection.


Allowed one letter codes:

A : Ala (Alanine)
C : Cys (Cysteine)
D : Asp (Aspartic Acid)
E : Glu (Glutamic Acid)
F : Phe (Phenylalanine)
G : Gly (Glycine)
H : His (Histidine)
I : Ile (Isoleucine)
K : Lys (Lysine)
L : Leu (Leucine)
M : Met (Methionine)
N : Asn (Asparagine)
P : Pro (Proline)
Q : Gln (Glutamine)
R : Arg (Arginine)
S : Ser (Serine)
T : Thr (Threonine)
V : Val (Valine)
W : Trp (Tryptophan)
X : Xaa (NNK - Any amino acid)
Y : Tyr (Tyrosine)
* : Ter (Termination)
Minimum Primer Length

The default minimum primer length is 15 nt. Raising this value
will increase the specificity of the primers. When modifications
are constrained to the 5′ tails, the minimum primer length
only applies to the annealing portion of the primer. To match the
specifications used in NEBaseChanger v1, set the minimum to 18 nt.
The minimum allowed value is 15 nt.
Minimum Primer Tm

The default minimum temperature for primer melting (Tm) is 55°C.
If higher primer binding specificity is desired or a tighter range
of Tm values across a larger set of primers is desired, raise the
minimum Tm value. Primer lengths will be longer at higher minimum
Tm values. The minimum allowed value is 55°C. Maximum allowed
value is 72°C.
Results

Successful primer generation output from NEBaseChanger can be viewed in multiple ways:

Required Primers Table

Displayed near the bottom of the page. In addition to the primer sequence,
the length, calculated melting temperature (Tm) and suggested
annealing temperature (Ta) are displayed. The primer display is automatically
updated whenever the mutation region or desired sequence is changed. Forward and
reverse primers are color coded and the 3-frame coding sequence is shown
allowing the user to verify that the desired mutation is incorporated.

Downloadable formats

Summary table
A tab-delimited table containing information comparable to the Primer Result table.
All primers
A tab-delimited plain text list of the required primers (name, sequence, note), suitable for common oligonucleotide order forms.
Selected primers
A tab-delimited plain text list of the required primers (name, sequence, note), suitable for common oligonucleotide order forms. Lited to just the selected primer pair.
All sequence
All result sequences in multi-FASTA format as a local text file.
Selected sequence
The result sequence for the selected primer pair in FASTA format as a local text file.

Use NEBuilder Calculator

NEBuilder Calculator (https://nebuildercalculator.neb.com) can be used to generate
a customized protocol for the NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix with calculated
optimal volumes of input DNA fragment sequences of each fragment.
The primers generated with the NEBuilder HiFi option selected are used to calculate
the expected PCR fragment lengths. This data is sent to NEBuilder Calculator
and opened in a new browser tab.
